prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system: continuous potable water, operator visibility, automatic control, manual intervention. Boundary: River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel to High Service Pump Header. Aliases: Ironwood=River Intake Pump Station (normally automatic; demand/channel depth govern starts; permissives: suction level, discharge path, healthy motor, open valves, no trips; start blocked on low Screen Channel level, drive fault, local control, unproven interlock; lost permissive: alarm/stop by severity). Lantern=SCADA Historian Server (trends, dose changes, analyzer values, filter status, wash sequences, operator comments; must retain accepted lab result timestamps with trend interval for audit reconciliation). Marigold=Coagulant Dosing Skid (automatic; sends Alum Batch Ticket on new lot; dose trimmed from analyzer feedback). Cobalt=North Filter Gallery (turbidity, headloss each scan). Sparrow=Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (custody receipt; sends Jar Test Photograph Set after date/time/ID check). Elements: Raw Water Screen Channel (sends Rake Torque Snapshot; high-high needs field confirmation); South Filter Gallery (sends Filter Run Exception Note); Clearwell Level Controller; Chlorine Contact Basin; Backwash Recovery Tank (sampled after return-to-process); High Service Pump Header. Items: Chlorine Residual Alarm (related grab samples prioritized). Requirements: manual override only when automatic unavailable; reason stated, restore automatic ASAP; large manual feed changes need Chief Operator approval; analyzer loss: hold last verified/fixed dose plus grab samples; filter return only when rinse-to-waste meets target; samples labeled at collection; field readings provisional until compared with lab; out-of-holding-time/temperature samples troubleshooting only, not compliance; QC (calibration, blanks, duplicates, standards) before release; failed-QC results flagged, corrected with justification or rejected; accepted results reconciled by time, point, process state, observations; Storm Intake Mode increases sampling until stable. Actors: Chief Operator (modes, targets, Storm Intake Mode, dose; notified when lab contradicts field-driven adjustment); Duty Engineer (configuration, forecasts, temporary dose; reviews significant field/lab differences); Laboratory Technician (verifies lot via Alum Batch Ticket; sends Sample Chain Slip; records label/log mismatches before acceptance; checks turbidity mixing/range and residual reagent/timing; preserves custody records); Distribution Dispatcher; Maintenance Planner; Chemical Supplier Driver; Residuals; regulatory auditors.

New part:
S101: Planned maintenance is controlled through a work order process that ties each task to an approved operating window, a named responsible person, and a defined return-to-service condition.
S102: The Chief Operator reviews the next-day schedule with operations staff so that treatment capacity, water quality risk, and distribution demand are understood before work is released.
S103: The Maintenance Planner is also known as Quarry for internal radio coordination during maintenance planning discussions.
S104: The Maintenance Planner verifies that each work order identifies affected equipment, required isolations, parts staging, and the evidence needed to close the work.
S105: The Maintenance Planner uses the snapshot to compare planned rake work against recent mechanical loading before releasing the task package.
S106: The Duty Engineer checks proposed work against current operating constraints and may defer nonessential activity when treatment margin is limited.
S107: Lockout planning identifies electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, chemical, and stored-energy hazards before personnel enter or service plant equipment.
S108: Field isolation is verified locally by the assigned craft worker and then acknowledged by operations before the equipment is opened, adjusted, or tested.
S109: Ironwood shall remain unavailable for routine maintenance release until isolation points are tagged, verified locally, and acknowledged in the shift turnover record.
S110: Work in the North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery is scheduled to keep enough filtration capacity available for expected demand and wash cycles.
S111: Any planned change affecting the Clearwell Level Controller requires coordination with the High Service Pump Header operating plan before the change is applied.
S112: The Chemical Supplier Driver sends the Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before unloading any replacement cylinders at the plant.
S113: Supplier access is limited to approved routes, assigned unloading areas, and times when an operator is available to observe chemical connections and vehicle movement.
S114: Deliveries for the Coagulant Dosing Skid are staged so that hoses, containment, and emergency washdown equipment are inspected before transfer begins.
S115: Chemical work near the Chlorine Contact Basin is coordinated with operating staff so that ventilation, gas monitoring, and communications are available during the task.
S116: Shift communication includes the status of open isolations, temporary operating limits, unavailable equipment, and any abnormal condition that could affect the next crew.
S117: The Distribution Dispatcher is informed before maintenance changes the availability of the High Service Pump Header, North Distribution Pressure Station, or South Distribution Pressure Station.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
